slides.headline: You've got a 900-day streak. You still can't order a coffee.
Apps taught you to tap.
slides.sub: Tap the right answer. Pick the picture. Match the pair. Four hundred times, in the right order.

slides.headline: Nobody taught you to answer.
slides.sub: Someone asks you something out loud and your mind goes blank. Not because you don't know the words. Because you've never had to say them.

slides.headline: So Sayla calls you.
slides.sub: A real voice on the phone. It asks something simple, then it waits. No buttons. No multiple choice. Nowhere to hide.

slides.headline: The first call is uncomfortable.
slides.sub: The second one isn't. By the fifth you stop translating in your head and start just talking.

slides.headline: Ten minutes. Phone to your ear. No screen.
slides.sub: That's the whole practice. It's the part every other app skips.

slides.headline: Speak first. Study later.
slides.sub: A language you can use is one you've said out loud, badly, to someone who answers.
